Window Cleaning in Kennewick Is Really Two Jobs

Ask a Kennewick window cleaner what they spend their time on and you'll get two answers, and neither is ordinary dirt. The first is dust film — the fine silt that wind deposits on glass in a translucent haze, most visible when low winter sun hits a west window. The second is hard-water spotting, and it's the tougher opponent: sprinkler overspray carrying Columbia Basin minerals dries on glass, and after enough cycles the deposits etch in. A window that's been sprinkler-sprayed all summer doesn't wipe clean; it needs mineral-dissolving treatment, and in bad cases the etching is permanent.

That second problem is why local pros ask about your irrigation before they quote. Adjusting one rogue sprinkler head costs nothing and saves the glass; cleaning spots annually while the sprinkler keeps spraying is a subscription to a solvable problem. The dust film, meanwhile, is simply the price of desert living — most Kennewick homes look noticeably sharper with two washes a year, spring (post-wind-season) and fall.

For homes, storefronts, and post-construction cleans, we can connect you with window cleaning pros working across the Tri-Cities.

Common window cleaning situations in Kennewick

Hard-water spots that won't wipe off

White spotting concentrated on lower panes near lawn edges is sprinkler mineral residue. Fresh deposits respond to acidic cleaners and polishing; years-old deposits may be etched into the glass itself. A pro can tell you which you have in about ten seconds — and which sprinkler head to blame.

Wind-season grit in tracks and screens

Window tracks in Kennewick collect a mortar of silt, and screens load with enough fine dust to visibly gray the view. Track detailing and screen washing are the add-ons that make a local window clean feel transformative rather than cosmetic.

Post-construction windows in new developments

New builds and remodels leave stucco splatter, paint flecks, and sticker residue that ordinary washing won't touch. Construction cleans involve razor work that must be done correctly — tempered glass can scratch if scraped wrong — which is exactly why this is professional territory.

How it works

  1. 1

    Count, condition, and quote

    Pricing goes by pane count, stories, and condition — with a hard-water assessment separating standard washing from restoration work. Photos by text often get you a solid quote without a visit.

  2. 2

    Wash — the right method for the glass

    Traditional squeegee work for spotted or filmed glass; water-fed pole systems with purified water for upper stories and maintenance cleans. Purified water matters here: rinsing with mineral-heavy tap water just reapplies the spots.

  3. 3

    Tracks, screens, sills

    The full-service version vacuums and wipes tracks, washes screens, and details sills — the difference between clean glass and clean windows in a dusty climate.

  4. 4

    Prevention notes

    A good pro leaves you with specifics: which sprinkler heads hit glass, whether a hydrophobic coating is worth it on problem panes, and a realistic schedule for your exposure.

What window cleaning costs in Kennewick

Residential window cleaning in the Tri-Cities is quoted per pane or per home size, with single-story ranches — the local staple — at the friendly end and two-story homes adding ladder or pole premiums. Interior-and-exterior costs roughly half again more than exterior-only. Hard-water restoration is separate, priced by severity per pane, and genuinely etched glass is a replacement conversation, not a cleaning one. Storefront routes run on weekly or monthly subscription pricing that's modest per visit.

Frequently asked questions

How do I stop sprinklers from spotting my windows?

Audit the system on a calm morning: watch a full cycle and flag any head whose spray or drift reaches glass. Most fixes are head adjustments or swaps to lower-angle nozzles — minutes of work. Where overlap is unavoidable, a hydrophobic glass coating makes deposits rinse off more easily.

How often do Kennewick windows need professional cleaning?

Twice a year suits most homes: after spring wind season and again in fall. Homes on busy roads, near construction, or with heavy irrigation exposure often go quarterly. Skipping years lets hard-water deposits age toward permanence, which is the expensive path.

Can old hard-water stains be removed from glass?

Fresh-to-middle-aged deposits, yes — acid-based mineral removers and cerium oxide polishing restore most panes. Deposits that have chemically etched the glass surface leave permanent ghosting. The honest quote distinguishes restorable panes from replacement candidates.

Do pros clean windows in winter here?

Yes — Kennewick winters are workable apart from hard-freeze days, and winter light is exactly when dust film shows most. Cleaners use cold-weather additives to keep solution from freezing on the glass.

What's a water-fed pole and is it as good as hand washing?

A brush on a telescoping pole fed with purified water — it scrubs and rinses spot-free without ladders, making second stories fast and safe. For maintenance cleans it matches hand work; for first-time cleans of filmed or spotted glass, traditional squeegee-and-detail still wins.
